issues.title: Extra selectivity for HAVING-style aggregate-result range filters in join ordering
issues.hypothesis: In q18 the customer HASH_JOIN costs 0.39s CPU plus 0.12s for the customer scan, about 55 ms of wall time. Measured: full q18 is about 577 ms, the variant without customer about 522 ms, the aggregate alone about 470 ms. That join builds a 1.5M-row hash table (keys span 1.5M values, above PerfectHashJoinExecutor MAX_BUILD_SIZE=1048576, so no perfect HJ) and is probed by only 111 rows. Customer is chosen as the build side because the SEMI-joined orders side is estimated at ~3.5M rows. The IN-subquery is Projection->Filter(sum(x) > c)->Aggregate(~14M groups), and the HAVING filter gets only the generic DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY 0.2 (relation_manager.cpp:274-277, aggregate case in ExtractJoinRelations). A hand-written variant that caps that side (LIMIT 100000, results identical) makes the optimizer build on the small side and probe customer. Alternating runs: 511/551 ms vs 551/574 ms for the original, about -5%. Filters on group keys are normally pushed below the aggregate, so the filters that stay above it are mostly range predicates on aggregate results (heavy-hitter or tail filters such as sum > c or count >= c). These usually keep a small fraction of the groups, so 0.2 is too generous.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/join_order/relation_manager.cpp, ExtractJoinRelations, case LOGICAL_AGGREGATE_AND_GROUP_BY (around line 265): after ExtractAggregationStats and the existing `if (!datasource_filters.empty())` multiplication by DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY, add a static helper `FilterHasAggregateRangePredicate(datasource_filters, aggr.aggregate_index)`. It walks each LogicalFilter's expressions and their AND conjunctions. It returns true if some conjunct is a BoundComparisonExpression of type GREATERTHAN/GREATERTHANOREQUALTO/LESSTHAN/LESSTHANOREQUALTO where one side is a BoundColumnRefExpression with binding.table_index == aggr.aggregate_index and the other side IsFoldable(). If it returns true, multiply operator_stats.cardinality by DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY once more (at most once in total), clamped to >= 1. Do NOT change aggr.SetEstimatedCardinality (the aggregate's own estimate stays). Use LossyNumericCast like the surrounding code. Verify with EXPLAIN on q18 that customer becomes the probe side of its join (the ~111-row side should build) and that the lineitem join still builds on the small side. Then bench q18. If the flip does not happen, print the semi-RHS estimate and check that the filter really is in datasource_filters for this aggregate (the RHS goes through LOGICAL_PROJECTION -> AddRelationWithChildren -> child optimizer). If needed, also consider the equivalent path at line 198. No setting or default changes.
issues.expected_gain: q18: -5..-8% (customer build of ~0.4s CPU replaced by probing 1.5M rows against a ~111-row table)
issues.generality: Any query that joins an IN/EXISTS subquery or derived table with a HAVING range predicate on an aggregate (top spenders, groups with count > N, large orders) to other tables. The smaller estimate lets the join order put that side on the build side and probe the big dimension. Queries whose HAVING keeps most groups could get a worse join order: they would build on a side that is larger than estimated. Results stay correct because only estimates change.
issues.risk: Low for correctness (only cardinality estimates change). Medium for plan regressions on hidden queries with non-selective HAVING clauses. Also check that the expression walk handles nested conjunctions and casts on the column side (it can simply not match).

issues.title: Allow more zonemap ranges than dynamic_or_filter_threshold in key-range join filter
issues.hypothesis: E0005 pushes at most 50 merged ranges for about 111 keys. The lineitem probe scan still emits 17.5M of 60M rows, while with one key per row group about 13.6M would be the floor. Checking a row group against a range set is cheap, so a separate cap (for example 1024 ranges, binary search over sorted ranges) would prune more.
issues.plan: physical_hash_join.cpp range-set path from E0005: use its own constexpr cap on the number of ranges instead of dynamic_or_filter_threshold. Possibly also replace the OR-of-ranges filter with a sorted-range filter that checks statistics by binary search.
issues.generality: Hash joins with a small, scattered build key set over clustered probe tables.
issues.risk: Low; the gain is probably below noise.
